name: Kansas City
tagline: Low and slow, and worth every minute
description: A river-town crossroads where jazz was rewritten after dark and barbecue got its own dialect. Kansas City runs on patience — the kind that turns tough brisket into burnt ends and a Tuesday night into a jam session that outlasts the band. Between the fountains and the smokestacks you'll find world-class art hung for free, a jazz district that birthed Charlie Parker, and a fan base that turns fall Sundays into a red sea. Come hungry, stay curious, and let the city cook.

known_for: the Nelson-Atkins and free world-class art
identity.vibe: Unhurried, warm, and quietly proud — a working city that lets the good stuff take its time

hero.summer: The ballpark lights hum, Boulevardia spills down the boulevards, and the smokers never cool off — summer here is a long, sweaty, glorious cookout.
hero.fall: Red and gold everywhere you look — the leaves, the Chiefs jerseys, the burnt ends caramelizing in the pit while the whole city holds its breath for Sunday.
hero.winter: Cold nights are what jazz was made for — duck into a warm room off 18th & Vine, order something smoked, and let the low-and-slow season keep you.
hero.spring: First pitch weather: patios reopen, the fountains switch back on, and the city stretches awake with a plate of ribs and a hopeful scorecard.

nexus.description: Ground zero for Kansas City's soul — the historic Black cultural and jazz district where Charlie Parker came up and the American Jazz Museum and Negro Leagues Baseball Museum share a roof. From here the BBQ lineage runs straight back into the same neighborhoods. This is where the story starts: 18th & Vine to the pit.

nexus_grid.title: American Jazz Museum
nexus_grid.description: Interactive exhibits on Parker, Ellington, and Ella, plus the working Blue Room club and the restored Gem Theater — jazz you can hear, not just read about.

nexus_grid.title: Negro Leagues Baseball Museum
nexus_grid.description: The definitive telling of Black baseball, right where the Monarchs played — a companion to the jazz museum under the same 18th & Vine roof.

nexus_grid.title: The Burnt-End Trail
nexus_grid.description: The BBQ lineage that grew out of these same blocks — brisket points burnt low and slow into the city's signature bite. Follow your nose.

nexus_grid.title: The Blue Room
nexus_grid.description: A jazz club that doubles as a museum by day and a live room by night — Mondays, Fridays, and Saturdays the horns come out.

nexus_grid.title: Gem Theater
nexus_grid.description: The 1912 movie house reborn as a performing-arts stage anchoring the district's south side — concerts, film, and jazz history in one room.

nexus_grid.title: Mutual Musicians Foundation
nexus_grid.description: The legendary after-hours union hall where KC jam sessions still run past 1 a.m. — a National Historic Landmark that never fully stopped swinging.

modes.label: Foodie
modes.description: Burnt ends, ribs, and the great sauce debate — plus a new-school food scene that's earned its own smoke ring.

modes.label: Chill
modes.description: Slow mornings in the coffee houses, easy afternoons in the sculpture park — the city's default gear is unhurried.

modes.label: Romantic
modes.description: Fountains at dusk, a candlelit table, and a jazz club nightcap — KC does low-lit and lovely better than it lets on.

modes.label: Adventurer
modes.description: River trails, streetcar sprints, and day-trip escapes to Lawrence or Weston — plenty to roam beyond downtown.

modes.label: Culture
modes.description: 18th & Vine, the free Nelson-Atkins, and the WWI Museum's 217-foot tower — a city that punches way above its size on the arts.

modes.label: Nightlife
modes.description: After-hours jam sessions, Power & Light crowds, and rooftop bars — the horns and the taps stay on late.

modes.label: Family
modes.description: Ballgames, the zoo, science center, and the fountains kids can chase — easy wins for the whole crew.

transit.from_nearest_hub: Kansas City International Airport (MCI) sits about 20 miles northwest of downtown — roughly 25-30 minutes by car or rideshare. The airport's single modern terminal opened in 2023.
transit.local_transport: The free KC Streetcar runs the north-south downtown spine from the River Market through the Crossroads to Union Station and now Country Club Plaza. RideKC buses cover the rest, but a car earns its keep for the museums, 18th & Vine, and any BBQ pilgrimage off the streetcar line.

side_trips.name: Lawrence, Kansas
side_trips.pitch: A leafy college town with an outsized indie streak — bookshops, live music, and a Massachusetts Street that actually walks.

side_trips.name: Weston, Missouri
side_trips.pitch: A preserved 1800s river town of antique shops, wineries, and a distillery — the slow-Sunday antidote to the city.

concierge.name: The Pitmaster
concierge.greeting: Well, look who wandered in. Grab a stool — the good stuff takes time, and I've got plenty of it. Tell me what you're hungry for, and I don't just mean the ribs.
concierge.personality: Patient, warm, and wry — talks about the city the way he tends a smoker: low and slow, no rushing the bark. Evenhanded in the eternal burnt-end debates, generous with a story, and quietly certain that anything worth having is worth waiting on.
concierge.sign_off: Now go on — pace yourself, save room, and let the city cook. I'll keep the pit warm.
